result.summary: The image shows a narrow residential street with row houses and parallel parking on both sides. The sidewalks are present but extremely narrow and lack any buffer from the roadway, creating a constrained environment for pedestrians. While the narrow street width likely limits vehicle speeds, the lack of pedestrian space and visibility issues from parked cars are notable concerns.

hazards.name: Narrow Sidewalks
hazards.description: The sidewalks are very narrow, making it difficult for pedestrians to pass each other or use mobility devices.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the street in the foreground and midground

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked cars on both sides of the narrow street significantly limit sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the street

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Expand the sidewalk width by reallocating space from the parking lane to improve pedestrian mobility and accessibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near intersections or mid-block points to improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The image shows a typical urban residential environment with a continuous concrete sidewalk directly adjacent to the curb. While the walkway is in good condition, there is no physical buffer between pedestrians and the roadway, and parked vehicles create visual obstructions.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb block the line of sight between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and right side of the image

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the curb with no planting strip or furniture zone to separate pedestrians from traffic.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Introduce a planting zone between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Daylighting)
interventions.description: While not an intersection, ensuring clear sightlines at nearby crossing points by restricting parking near corners would improve safety.

result.summary: The image shows a typical urban mixed-use environment with continuous sidewalks and a signalized intersection. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like marked crosswalks and signals are present, the street lacks modern safety enhancements such as curb extensions or dedicated buffers between the walkway and moving traffic.

hazards.name: Intersection Visibility
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corners may obstruct sightlines between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection near the red fire hydrant

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the curb with no planting strip or physical barrier to separate pedestrians from moving traffic.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility for all users.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to ensure clear sightlines between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade the standard transverse markings to continental or ladder-style markings to increase visibility to drivers.

result.summary: The image depicts a narrow urban sidewalk in front of a mixed-use building with a diner on the ground floor. The pedestrian environment is constrained by sidewalk obstructions such as trash bins and boxes, and there is no physical buffer between the walkway and the adjacent parking/travel lane.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Trash bins and cardboard boxes are placed directly on the walkway, significantly narrowing the effective width for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the sidewalk in front of the grey wall section

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: The presence of a vehicle parked immediately adjacent to the sidewalk blocks sightlines between pedestrians and any moving traffic.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Clearance and Management
interventions.description: Implement and enforce regulations regarding the placement of commercial waste and storage on the public right-of-way to maintain a clear walking path.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and personal security for pedestrians during evening hours.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: If this were near an intersection, curb extensions would improve sightlines and reduce crossing distances, though mid-block they could also be used to protect the tree and create dedicated space for bins.
